title: Staged quantized rollout with automated safety‑net rollback for calibration/regression detection
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Goal: Implement a staged (multi-step) rollout for quantized model variants (FP8/INT8) that performs calibration and accuracy validation against a held-out prompt set at each stage, and automatically triggers a safety‑net rollback to the previous higher-precision model when quality checks fail.

Problem: We frequently see small accuracy regressions after aggressive quantization (especially FP8 kernels on long-context workloads). Manual rollouts are slow and error-prone; ops teams need an automated guardrail that validates quality metrics during a canary/staged rollout and re-routes traffic on failure without developer intervention.

Approach overview:
- Define quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) as first-class artifacts with associated calibration metadata (scale factors, per-layer histograms, calibration inputs).
- Extend the calibration pipeline to emit a compact validation signature: sample-level EM/F1/ROUGE deltas, embedding cosine similarity distribution, and categorical failure flags for hallucination heuristics.
- Implement staged rollout controller: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (configurable). Each stage runs a background validation job comparing live-sampled requests + offline held-out prompt set against baseline model.
- Automated safety-net rollback: On threshold breach (configurable e.g., >2% EM regression absolute or >99th percentile embedding cosine shift) the controller immediately routes traffic back to the last known-good model and marks the quantized variant as failed.
- Observability: add per-variant dashboards (latency, cost delta, validation metrics, sample traces) and alerting (pager for P0 regressions, slack for P1).
- API/Config: expose rollout policies and validation thresholds via the admin API and console, and support per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Risks & trade-offs:
- False positives from noisy live samples -> mitigate by combining offline held-out validation with live-sampled aggregated metrics and conservative early thresholds.
- Extra cost from parallel validation runs during rollout; provide optional 'quick' mode that uses a smaller calibration set.
- Rollback speed vs stability: immediate rollback reduces customer-facing regressions but may mask recoverable transient noise. Provide cooldown windows and human review flags.

Deliverables:
- Calibration metadata spec and storage schema for quantization profiles.
- Validation harness that outputs a compact signature and pass/fail verdict.
- Staged rollout controller implementation and console controls.
- Telemetry & dashboards + runbook for rollback incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Quantization profile schema defined and stored in model catalog with calibration metadata
Calibration pipeline produces validation signature and store of per-release validation artifacts
Staged rollout controller supports at least 4 stages and configurable thresholds
Automated rollback triggers when validation thresholds are violated and routes traffic to last-good model within SLA window
Console exposes rollout policy and pass/fail reason in the model variant UI
End-to-end e2e test that simulates an intentional accuracy regression triggers rollback in CI
Dashboard shows per-variant validation metrics, latency, and cost delta
